The Neighborhood: Platt Park
At the turn of the 20th century, the Platt Park neighborhood—then a separate city from Denver—was a bustling borough of five-and-dime shops and sprawling family homes connected to the city by a clanking trolley line that ran up Pearl Street. As the Mile High City grew, the neighborhood was incorporated, and Denverites migrated south to make it their home. Today, the neighborhood’s storied history is still visible on Pearl Street, where visitors can glimpse trolley tracks peeking through the asphalt overlay, and new shops and purveyors occupy the original, historic buildings.

neighborhood_overview:
One of the coolest and most conveniently located neighborhoods in Denver, this house is right off 6th and I-25, yet far enough from traffic to be quiet and homey.
The Santa Fe Arts District isn't as polished and gentrified as many other neighborhoods in Denver. No big chains and fast-food restaurants on Santa Fe or South Broadway, but plenty of breweries, restaurants, theatres, and more!
One caveat, the neighbors on both sides are musicians. I've never had any noise complaints from tenants, but want to warn those who may be light sleepers or sensitive to noise, this Art District home may not be right for you (especially on the first friday of the month).

name: Urban Nest in heart of Denver
neighborhood_overview: This is one of the oldest neighborhoods of Denver. All the houses have character and charm. It is fun just to go for a walk. We live just a block from many great restaurants, and our go- to coffee shop "St Marks". There are restaurants all along 17th street! Just 5 blocks from both - City Park and Cheeseman Park, where we love to take the dogs, go for a run, rent a bike or paddle boat for an hour or so, or picnic on a summer sunday night to listen to live music. The Zoo and Botanic Gardens are in walking distance. During the summer months the Botanic Gardens hosts amazing, intimate concerts in their outdoor amphitheater. If you're here during this time you should check out their calendar. There are several other concert venues in close proximity, too. Less then a 10 minute commute to both Downtown Denver and Cherry Creek North or Cherry Creek Mall. Close to several other old town neighborhoods with small shops and tons of restaurants.

Grub: Head to the French-inspired Vert Kitchen for homemade sandwiches (try the curried chicken), or a fast-casual brunch. (Or not so casual: They also sell bottles of champagne.) Wash Park West is also a great destination for Asian cuisine, and Thai Basil, although a chain, serves up the best green curry in that neighborhood. Next door, Fontana Sushi rolls up creative specials, like the Spiderman, which adds extra crab, spicy mayo, and eel sauce to the already scrumptious Spider roll.

name: Denver's Urban Oasis + Hot Tub
neighborhood_overview:
Jefferson Park is a fantastic neighborhood -- a safe one, with lots of history as well as brand new development. Within just a few blocks you'll find excellent bars and dining, including Araujo’s, Ros Siam Thai, Red Tops, Curry & Grill, Briar Commons, Chili Verde, Snarf's (and Snarfburger!), The Federal Bar & Grille, Jefferson Park Pub, Sweet Action Ice Cream, 2914 Coffee, and Sexy Pizza. It's a short walk to Broncos games at Empower Field. Great Denver attractions like Meow Wolf, the Downtown Aquarium, Children's Museum, and Jefferson and Confluence Parks are also easily reached on foot. There's a major grocery store (with one of the area’s cheaper gas stations) just two blocks away. Super easy access to I-25 and I-70, too!

Further afoot, a longer walk or fun bike ride gets you into downtown Denver, LoHi, the Highlands, West Highlands, Sloan's Lake, or the CU Denver/Metro State U campus.

neighborhood_overview:
Make yourself at home and relax, you are among friends and neighbors!

Barbershop and one day spa are also down Sheridan just past Starbucks, as is Northern Lights dispensary. The other way on 29th is my favorite day spa A new spirit 4840 w. 29th.
Catch the #28 Eastbound bus in the covered bus shed by the lake across the street from 7-11. Fare is $2.60 and includes a transfer. This takes you downtown where you can catch the free 16th St. Mall Shuttle. Catch the #28 bus Westbound to return home on 15th St. The drivers are all very helpful as are other riders.

name: Remodeled Old-World Home in Downtown Denver
neighborhood_overview:
Five points is a beloved old neighborhood in Denver. Situated in a prime location between RiNo and LoDo. It's a great place to see shows, hop around local breweries, and enjoy local art. The Curtis Park Deli is right around the corner, British Bulldog is right down the street, and with a short walk, scooter or Uber you can be at many of Denver's best restaurants, bars, and entertainment areas.

As this house is at the heart of the city, you will hear city noises, including emergency vehicles at times during your stay. Also, it is only a few blocks from the mission, so there are quite a few homeless persons in the area. I've never experienced any issues with them in the year I've lived here.

name: Sloans Lake Row Home w/ Patio & Grill!
neighborhood_overview:
The Sloan's Lake neighborhood is one of Denver's newest hot spots and Sloan’s Lake is within walking distance, just a few blocks away (across Colfax).

After a stroll along the lake, head to one of the nearby restaurants or cafés: The Patio, Odell Brewing, or ChoLon — or catch a movie at the renowned Alamo Drafthouse!

The historic Edgewater neighborhood is just west of the lake with even more great local attractions, including Rupert’s, Joyride and Sloan’s Bar.

The Highlands neighborhood is a 10 minute ride, as well as the ballpark & other downtown attractions. Empower Field at Mile high, home of the Denver Broncos, is less than a mile away.

I25 is 2 miles down Colfax - Jump on 6 to Red Rocks (a quick 20 minute drive) or to the surrounding area for some beautiful Colorado scenery in the foothills of the Rocky Mountains.

The local brewery, Seedstock, is three doors down from the house & you can often find food trucks outside.

Directly to the west is the lovely Johnson and Wales campus just two blocks away, and Park Hill, one of Denver's oldest and most elegant neighborhoods is also to the west. Park Hill features some lovely parkways, including 17th Street, Montview Boulevard, 23rd Street and Monaco Boulevard; it is a nice place to walk. (And if you're really motivated, the Zoo, City Park and Museum of Nature and Science are about 2.5 miles west.)
To the north and south are the relatively newer neighborhoods of Stapleton and Lowry, with town centers, restaurants and cafes.
Going to the east, the neighborhoods are more transitional, but changing fast as they are now anchored by the newer and huge Anshutz Medical Campus. Not to be missed is the spanking new Stanley Marketplace, housed in a former airplane factory, with brewpubs and some of the most innovative new restaurants in Denver. name: Rococo Romance: 2 Bedroom Cap Hill
neighborhood_overview: Capitol Hill is a quintessential Denver neighborhood, a place where politicos and hipsters cross paths. It is Denver's most densely populated neighborhood. It was once the home of Denver's elite and origination of Foursquare architecture in Denver. Today it consists of historic mansions, apartments and condo buildings. Because of the concentration of multi-family uses and the urban character of the neighborhood, parking is at a premium. The area is strongly influenced by the Colorado State Capitol and Downtown Denver which is adjacent to the northwest boundary of the neighborhood. Commercial uses are typically located on major arterials such as Colfax Avenue, East 8th Avenue, East 14th Avenue, East 13th Avenue, Lincoln Street and Broadway. A considerable number of mansion properties have been converted to office uses over the past several years due to zoning exemptions offered to historic structures which are zoned for residential uses.

We are in the city! The neighborhood is a mix of residents who are third and fourth generation, new additions to the hip new restaurant and art scene as well as a fair number of Denver's transient/vagrant population- as is the case with most larger cities in this day and age. We haven't had any safety issues at the house, but please use common sense and keep doors locked and gates closed. Also, we encourage not leaving anything in vehicles.

neighborhood_overview:
NEIGHBORHOOD/LOCATION
Our house is in South Park Hill, one of Denver's established residential neighborhoods. The streets are lined with large trees and mostly single family houses. The neighborhood is safe, relatively quiet, and surprisingly close to downtown.

Park Hill is on the edge of Denver's largest park -- the one with the zoo and nature and science museum in it.

The view from behind the museum is iconic: lake, park, skyline, and mountains. Watching the sunset (or even the reflection of the sunrise) from here is sublime.

There's also a large water feature behind the museum for kids to play in during the summer and paddle boats and surreys to rent from a stand near the park pavilion.

For runners, there is a 5K path that winds through the park; the outside of the park is 3 miles long -- 3.5 miles if you go around the golf course.

name: Downtown Denver Victorian 1-Bedroom Apartment
neighborhood_overview:
The property is located in one of the oldest neighborhoods in Denver - at edges of the Curtis Park, San Rafael and Clements Historic Districts - all of which are dominated by beautifully restored Victorian 1880's homes.

Clements Historic District typifies high-style Queen Anne and Italianate architecture, and is one of the most intact collections of late 19th Century Victorian high-style residential architecture in Denver. It is representative of the City’s rapid growth and middle class population of the 19th Century. The district maintains beautiful views of the Rocky Mountains to the west.

Curtis Park, Denver’s first street car suburb, is one of the city’s oldest and most diverse residential areas. The neighborhood’s heyday was from the late 1870s until 1893. The district is a showcase of architectural styles from that era, including Italianate, Eastlake, Queen Anne, and Victorian eclectic homes. neighborhood_overview:

Known for its eclectic mix of art, culture, and urban living, this neighborhood is an artistic and culinary mecca that will make your stay truly unforgettable.

Artistic Vibes: RiNo is Denver's premier art district, and you'll be surrounded by mesmerizing street art and colorful murals at every turn. Stroll down the streets and alleys to discover stunning graffiti, sculptures, and inspiring art installations. You'll quickly see why RiNo is often described as an open-air art gallery.

Craft Breweries: Craft beer enthusiasts, you're in for a treat! RiNo is home to numerous award-winning breweries and taprooms. Sip on unique, locally brewed beers while soaking up the lively atmosphere. Be sure to explore the RiNo Beer Trail for a taste of the best of Denver's craft beer scene.

Denver’s South Broadway neighborhood, affectionately known as SoBo, has grown from a major artery into downtown to an eclectic and funky mix of taverns, clothing stores, unique eateries, bookstores and hip, live music venues with rainbow crosswalks and dedicated bike lanes. From craft breweries, distilleries and cideries to sundrenched, rooftop patios, South Broadway thrives on the unique energy of its residents and visitors.

Home to Antique Row, South Broadway is not only a destination for pieces from the 17th century, but also for immersive art experiences at vibrant, independent galleries. Check out Turn of the Century Antiques for dolls and toys and Spectra Art Space for contemporary art pieces in a fun, welcoming environment.

A construction boom has also characterized the Sloan's Lake neighborhood in recent years, with a flurry of both single-family homes and apartment units being built. Along Tennyson Street between West 44th Avenue and West 38th Avenue, you'll find a host of fun places to visit, such as the Denver Cat Company, a feline-friendly lounge that serves coffee, pastries and bagels, as well as plenty of coffee shops (like Downpours Coffee and Allegro Coffee Roasters Tennyson). neighborhood_overview: ELEGANT & HISTORIC, MONTCLAIR --  Denver's  Montclair neighborhood is lined with brick homes, tree-lined avenues, and eccentric local businesses. Montclair is the brainchild of Baron Walter von Richthofen, a Prussian aristocrat and the uncle of famed WWI German pilot "Red Baron" Manfred von Richthofen who wanted an "utopian community" built on what were at the time empty fields east of Denver.  He started in 1887 with building what is now known as the community's centerpiece, the 14,938-square-foot limestone Richthofen Castle, located at 7020 E. 12th Ave.  My husband and I feel lucky to live here in Montclair with its beautiful homes and quiet and peaceful neighborhood, but we acknowledge that our "Utopia" has to evolve to include all souls.

name: A luxurious stay at modern 4-story Home (RiNo)
neighborhood_overview:
This property is amazing all year round for a visit to Denver.

The River North Art District "where art is made" goes by the nickname of "RiNo" and has even adopted a rhino design for its official logo, so look for creative rhinos in art and signage all around the neighborhood! The district's interesting blend of urban charm and unique industrial revival makes it a great destination. Historic warehouses and factories now house jazz bars, restaurants, brewpubs, art galleries and working studios. RiNo boasts a diverse mix of creative businesses ranging from visual artists, designers and furniture makers, to craft distillers and brewers, winemakers, creators of unique outdoor gear and small-batch coffee roasters. The art definitely extends beyond gallery walls in this neighborhood, with its colorful and innovative street art murals in alleys and on buildings around almost every corner! Home to everything from music venues, restaurants, breweries, and a plethora of art galleries

Foodies will also find plenty to love in RiNo, with various trendy restaurants and breweries. From upscale eateries to casual gastropubs, there's something for every taste and budget.

In addition to its artistic and culinary offerings, RiNo is also home to several unique shops and boutiques and a thriving nightlife scene. You'll be able to catch live music at one of the neighborhood's music venues or enjoy a cocktail at one of its many bars.

Colloquially known as West Wash Park, the neighborhood is heavily residential, filled with early-20th century houses that have been turned into multi-unit rentals, and offers easy access to a variety of essential and just-for-fun amenities. Whether you’re a city dweller searching for a new date-night spot, or a Sunday volleyball player looking for a new place to fuel up and wind down after summer games, this residential stalwart offers many fun ways to recharge your routine.

neighborhood_overview:
Curtis Park is the original neighborhood in Denver. Come check out beautiful Victorian homes and the neighborhood that started it all. Come for a vacation, leave with a history lesson.

Curtis Park is the creation of the city's first golden age, that time between 1870, when the railroad came to town, and 1893, when the Silver Crash brought a rude end to Denver's early prosperity. During that brief period, the rate of Denver's population growth was higher than that of any other city in the country. From a modest 4,759 in 1870, just twenty years later, in 1890, the city had 106,713 inhabitants. One historian has called it an "instant city."

The illustrated signs tell stories about people, places and ideas that helped shape African American culture and history in Denver.

neighborhood_overview:
Eat & Drink

The Highlands has one of the highest numbers of food and beverage offerings per capita of any neighborhood in Denver. The area is home to celebrated local restaurants like Spuntino and Cart-Diver; one of the city’s first food halls, Avanti Food & Beverage; and trendy additions such as Daughter Thai Kitchen & Bar and Señor Bear.

That doesn’t mean you can’t find history here. Lechuga’s Italian Restaurant has been around since 1961, and My Brother’s Bar (add a burger to your beer order) is the city’s oldest bar—it’s been operating since 1873.

Imbibers can stroll almost anywhere in the ’hood and find plenty of venues to enjoy craft brews (Denver Beer Co.) or craft cocktails (Lady Jane, Room for Milly) or locally made spirits (Mythology Distillery, the Family Jones Spirit House) or coffee (Queensberry Coffee, Pinwheel Coffee).

name: The Botanic — Designer Green Room by RiNo
neighborhood_overview:
The Botanic is in the NE corner of downtown Denver, nestled by a small park on a relatively side cul-de-sac within the historic neighborhood of Whittier. This location offers the best of both worlds: near instant access to the vibrancy of downtown life and the ability to easily retreat from the bustle of it all. Street art and craft brewery fans can walk to the neighboring communities of RiNo and Five Points within minutes to discover countless murals and distilleries that have put Denver on the map. Other popular spots such as LoHi, Ballpark, and City Park are also a quick drive away.

For concertgoers, Denver's two newest venues, Mission Ballroom and Number Thirty Eight are less than 10 minutes away. The Ogden, the Fillmore, the Bluebird and Denver Center for the Performing Arts are less than 15 minutes away.

For conference attendees, the Denver Convention Center is less than 15 minutes away and Gaylord Rockies Resort & Convention Center is about 25 minutes away.

Mar Lee is known for its concentration of Asian and Latinx restaurants and shops, its access to the mountains via Highway 6. There are restaurants, breweries, dispensaries, parks, and trails all nearby!

With our guests having access to the internet, we've built a house guide to highlight neighborhood gems and encourage folks to really experience the neighborhood in which they are staying. We've also noted BIPOC, women-owned, LGBTQA+-owned, and eco-friendly spots as supporting these businesses aligns with our values.

We acknowledge that our tiny home sits on the traditional lands of the Cheyenne and Ute peoples and we're committed to uplifting the name of these lands and the community members from these Nations who reside alongside us.

"Victorian-era homes and buildings; lush gardens and parks; hip independently owned shops; art galleries; and restaurants, all make the Denver Highlands neighborhood a great destination for visitors. There are three diverse districts to discover here: Highlands Square, Tennyson Street and Lower Highlands (LoHi). Boutiques, wine shops and bookstores, as well as popular restaurants and bars radiate out from Highland Square on West 32nd Avenue and Lowell Boulevard. And, in the Tennyson Street Cultural District, you can spend an afternoon browsing antique prints, photographs and paintings from Colorado artists, plus find live music venues and great ethnic foods. LoHi is characterized by a mix of old and ultra-modern architecture, some of the city's most innovative restaurants and bars, and incredible views of the Highland Bridge and downtown Denver."

Read more about the Highlands from the VISIT DENVER website.

If you're hungry you can dine at any one of our favorite restaurants like Park Burger, Kaos Pizza, Sexy Pizza, Sushi Den, Que Bueno Suerte or more than a dozen others. There are also plenty of great shops to peruse... with everything from clothing to books to musical instruments. You'll see why historic South Pearl is a favorite Denver destination.

The Denver Botanic Garden is next to Cheesman Park. A dispensary is located on 6th, three blocks away, close to a group of restaurants.

There’s good cycling in the area. The Cherry Creek trail is nearby and that runs 3 miles to downtown along the river, and ends where the creek meets the Platte River (at the REI store). In the other direction the Cherry Creek trail runs about 10 miles to the Reservoir / park, which has swimming and a beach. The trail is for cyclists and pedestrians- no cars and as the water is cold, it’s usually a pleasant ride on a hot day.
For nearby hiking trails a car is recommended. Walking to Cheesman park and around it and back is about 1.5 to 2 miles.

neighborhood_overview:
Sloan's Lake is a quiet and peaceful neighborhood located on the east and north shores of Sloan's Lake; the largest lake in the City of Denver and the second largest park. This neighborhood while being very quiet is close to many of Denver's trendiest places and has easy access to the highway system for travel and adventure in any direction.

name: Vibrant guest suite; great Denver location
neighborhood_overview:
Located in the northeastern part of the city, Denver's Cole neighborhood is a true example of a diverse neighborhood oasis in the heart of the city. While primarily residential, there are several bars, restaurants and stores within walking distance, and the neighborhood is situated between two new industrial redevelopments - Denver Rock Drill and York Street Yards, linked by the 39th Avenue Greenway Trail - which bring new food, drink and entertainment options to the neighborhood on seemingly a daily basis. The majority of homes in the neighborhood date to the early 1900s, and a walk down just about any street will highlight multiple different architectural styles.

Most importantly for travelers, the neighborhood provides easy transportation access via I-70 or the light rail to the airport, and close proximity to some of Denver's most exciting places to explore, all while providing a return to quiet, comfortable accommodations at the end of the day.

With close proximity to downtown, easy access to Sloan’s Lake, and both the Pepsi Center and Mile High Stadium in its back yard, you can see why West Colfax is officially on our radar.


While the distinction between the Sloan’s Lake neighborhood and West Colfax is often blurred, a few things set them apart. Sloan’s Lake is mostly single-family homes, while West Colfax has a more diverse mixture of mid-rise buildings, single-family homes, and a few brand-new condos. name: Spacious and stylish 1-bedroom with modern kitchen
neighborhood_overview:
Athmar Park is a hidden gem with a friendly, multicultural vibe. Walkable attractions include Chain Reaction Brewing Company (0.5 miles), beautiful Huston Lake Park (0.7 mi) and expansive Ruby Hill Park/Levitt Pavilion (1.4 mi). Huston Lake Park features mountain views, tennis and pickleball courts, a playground and a mile-long paved path around the water — also popular for fishing. In the warmer months Levitt Pavilion offers free concerts.

Directly south, City Park encompasses much more than just its namesake 314-acre park. It’s also home to the Denver Zoo and the Denver Museum of Nature & Science.

The Wash Park neighborhood has delicious restaurants, hip bars, and a family-friendly atmosphere. Wash Park itself has two lakes, two formal flower gardens, historic buildings, tennis courts, tree-lined paths and expanses of green grass. It's a fitness mecca for Denverites.

Nearby is South Pearl Street, once the site of the city's first trolley car route, now home to galleries, wine and cocktail bars, specialty shops, boutique and high-end clothing stores, and some of Denver's best local dining.

name: Adobe charm in the 7th Avenue Historic district
neighborhood_overview:
The 7th Avenue Historic District
From containing the residence of the Summer White House during the Eisenhower administration to being home of the inventor of the ice cream soda, the East 7th Avenue Historic District is one of the most interesting and beautiful in Denver.

Primarily built from the 1890’s to the 1930’s, the East 7th Avenue Historic District is the largest in Denver with its boundaries stretching from Logan Street to Colorado Avenue, and from 6th Avenue to 8th Avenue. Between Steele and Harrison Streets, the district is limited to the 7th Avenue Parkway. Because Downing Street was a main thoroughfare in the late 1890’s, the earliest construction in the district is found nearby on the 700 Blocks of Corona and Marion. 7th and Williams Street contained a stable for horses that used the Cheesman Esplanade, or “Little Cheesman”, for their exercising. name: 3 Bedroom Basement Bungalow next to Cheeseman Park
neighborhood_overview:
This unit is located only 40 minutes away from Denver International Airport and 10-15 minutes from other popular Denver neighborhoods like the Highlands, LoDo, RiNo, and Wash Park. Popular mountain resorts such as Vail or Breckenridge are about 1.5 hours away, and Colorado Springs is just over an hour. The Basement Bungalow is also close to a Bus To Show stop for any Red Rocks concert goers. This area is popular, and any ride share apps such as Uber or Lyft work well. There is also a bike lane right outside of the unit that stretches across the city.

Quintessential Cheeseman Park is a few blocks away and is a popular spot for Denverites in the summer to hang out or walk your dog, and a half mile walk to Colfax Avenue will get you to concert venues, bars, breweries, and other shops. The Botanical Gardens is also only a couple blocks away and is just as beautiful in the winter during the Blossom of Lights as it is in the spring.

name: Cute basement apartment in West Washington Park!
neighborhood_overview: West Washington Park: This petite neighborhood is considered one of Denver’s most livable spaces. The area has a bubble effect—it sits barely south of Baker’s booming neighborhood and South Broadway dives, west of the ever-busy Washington Park, and walking distance to South Pearl Street, but maintains the air of quiet suburbia perfectly suited for families and professionals. Colloquially known as West Wash Park, the neighborhood is heavily residential, filled with early-20th century houses that have been turned into multi-unit rentals, and offers easy access to a variety of essential and just-for-fun amenities. (Think: grocery stores and fitness clubs, and watering holes and music venues.) Whether you’re a city dweller searching for a new date-night spot, or a Sunday volleyball player looking for a new place to fuel up and wind down after summer games, this residential stalwart offers many fun ways to recharge your routine.

name: Private Room in Historic District Townhome
neighborhood_overview:
Uptown is one of Denver's more active central neighborhoods. Gilded Age mansions line the streets of the Swallow Hill Historic District (which we are in) and lots of shops, restaurants, breweries, coffee shops and bars can be found within a few blocks. Several music venues, gay bars and ethnic food options are within stone's throw. Not to mention City Park is a short drive for recreation. Marczyk's Fine Foods is a small high-end corner grocery just a block away and Natural Grocer's is a few blocks too (for bigger selection). Argonaut Liquor Store is huge (thing Wal-mart of alcohol) and is just a few blocks down.

17th Avenue is the main drag of the neighborhood. If you go just beyond 17th/Park, you'll find a great stretch of bars and restaurants (Dos Santos Mexican, White Pie, Thin Man and Reverence Brewery are a few favorites). name: Sunny 3-bedroom home in the heart of Denver/RiNo
neighborhood_overview:
This bright and sunny home is perfectly positioned on a pocket park between 3 of Denver's most popular restaurant/bar/art districts (RiNo, LoDo, and Five Points). The house provides easy access to more than 30 restaurants and bars, but is just far enough away to be peaceful and quiet. The walk from RiNo into downtown has become one of the highlights of a stay in Denver, thanks to the large murals that brighten the walls of this art district, and our home is in the perfect position to access it all. Public transportation is only blocks away, but a nice walk or e-scooter will probably be all you need.

FYI: it is important to note that all of the homes in this area are in an urban setting, and Denver has chosen (like Seatlle and Portland) to embrace their homeless population, so it is not uncommon to see some homelessness in the neighborhood. While I have never felt unsafe in this area, standard precautions used in any urban setting to should be used.

neighborhood_overview:
This property sits across the street from City Park Golf Course. City Park is a large public park located in Denver, Colorado. It is situated just east of downtown Denver and covers over 330 acres. The park features a wide variety of amenities, including a boathouse, a golf course, a recreation center, and a number of sports fields and courts. name: Redbrick Cottage / 2BDRM / Wash Park / Yard & Gym
neighborhood_overview:
Washington Park

You’ll be staying a mere 5-minute walk from the neighborhood’s lovely Washington park, a unique urban oasis popular with Denverites out for a jog or picnic. Dubbed "Wash Park" by locals, the area has a Rockwellian feel with its lush landscaping, awning-covered storefronts and family-friendly atmosphere. Washington Park itself has two lakes, two formal flower gardens, tree-lined paths and seemingly endless expanses of green grass. It's a fitness mecca for locals, and on any given day you're likely to spot people walking their dogs, running, biking, paddle boating or doing yoga.

It's no wonder that it's consistently chosen as Denver's favorite park. Nearby is South Pearl Street, once the site of the city's first trolley car route, now home to art, wine and cocktail bars, specialty shops, boutique and high-end clothing stores and some of Denver's best local dining. Visit Old South Gaylord where you can experience local restaurants, galleries and shops

name: Classic Victorian in the Heart of Denver
neighborhood_overview:
Five Points is in the heart of Denver! You will be able to walk to coffee shops and restaurants. The RTD is only one block away, making not having a car very easy!

Beyond that, you are in the Historic Five Points District. Cultures blend in historic Five Points, one of Denver's oldest and most diverse neighborhoods. The district was known as the "Harlem of the West" because it was a frequent stop for jazz greats including Billie Holiday, Louis Armstrong and Miles Davis, who played clubs like the Rossonian and the Rainbow Room. The neighborhood was also mentioned repeatedly in Jack Kerouac's "On the Road."

Today, historic Five Points' creativity and vibrancy live on in a fascinating fusion of old and new. Visitors can stop in at innovative coffeehouses and craft breweries, visit museums telling stories from the past, experience live music from all genres at independent music venues or eat at beloved soul food and barbecue institutions.

name: Lovely 2-bedroom house in Baker
neighborhood_overview:
A historic neighborhood made up of approximately 30 blocks, this area is a vibrant and diverse community filled with lots of character and a great central location to tons of entertainment and transportation.

This area is known for it’s older but charming homes, with many being built in the 1800’s. In 2000, Baker was granted as Baker Historic District as part of the historic Preservation effort of the city of Denver. The criteria for designation included historical figures that lived in the neighborhood and many popular architectural styles, with several buildings designed by prominent architects from a period of significance of 1873 to 1937.

With South Broadway being just steps away, there is great access to tons of eateries, shops, parks and bars. Baker is a super accessible area, being ranked as the 5th most walkable neighborhood in Denver. Besides having great proximity to walk places, there are two access points to jump on the light rail as well.

The River North Art District "where art is made" goes by the nickname of "RiNo" and has even adopted a rhino design for its official logo, so look for creative rhinos in art and signage all around the neighborhood! The district's interesting blend of urban charm and unique industrial revival makes it a great destination for visitors. Historic warehouses and factories now house jazz bars, restaurants, brewpubs, art galleries and working studios. RiNo boasts a diverse mix of creative businesses ranging from visual artists, designers and furniture makers, to craft distillers and brewers, winemakers, creators of unique outdoor gear and small-batch coffee roasters. The art definitely extends beyond gallery walls in this neighborhood, with its colorful and innovative street art murals in alleys and on buildings around almost every corner!

There are three diverse districts to discover: Highlands Square , Tennyson Street and Lower Highland (LoHi ).

Boutiques, wine shops and bookstores, as well as popular restaurants and bars radiate out from Highland Square on West 32nd Avenue and Lowell Boulevard. And, in the Tennyson Street Cultural District, you can spend an afternoon browsing antique prints, photographs and paintings from Colorado artists, plus find live music venues and great international foods. LoHi is characterized by a mix of old and ultra-modern architecture, some of the city's most innovative restaurants and bars and incredible views of the Highland Bridge and downtown Denver.

name: Walk to music, food, bars & coffee - 420, Turo
neighborhood_overview:
Our neighborhood is called City Park West. It's on the west side of City Park, just east of downtown.

Neighborhoods that are within walking/biking distance include: RiNo, Capitol Hill, Uptown, Whittier, Five Points, Cheesman Park, Congress Park.

Depending on how much you like to walk/bike, you could even get Downtown without a car.

Our house is 4 blocks from 17th Avenue, also known as Restaurant Row. 17th Avenue ends at the edge of downtown, and is lined with restaurants, bars, and coffee shops the whole way.

We are about 6 blocks from Colfax, which is also lined with bars, concert venues, dispensaries, shops, etc.

RiNo is a newer neighborhood that's become popular over the past decade or so. It's full of converted warehouses, and there is plenty to explore. It's definitely possible to walk there on a nice day, but you might also opt to ride share or rent a bike, then walk around once you're there.

neighborhood_overview:
In 1878, the American circus mogul P.T. Barnum of the Barnum and Bailey Circus bought 760 acres for just $11,000, and a few years later, the Barnum subdivision was platted.

Barnum's involvement with his namesake's development has become part of Denver folklore, especially in the durable legend of the showman's plan to establish a winter home for his circus in the city. In fact, Barnum never wintered his animals anywhere other than Connecticut or Florida, and the entertainment entrepreneur made just four documented trips to Colorado. Barnum sold as much of Barnum as possible before disposing of the remainder to his daughter, Helen Buchtel, for the price of one dollar. neighborhood_overview:
Eat & Drink

If we had to bet, we’d guess that Highland has one of the highest numbers of food and beverage offerings per capita of any neighborhood in Denver. The area is home to celebrated local restaurants like Spuntino and Cart-Diver; one of the city’s first food halls, Avanti Food & Beverage; and trendy additions such as Daughter Thai Kitchen & Bar and Señor Bear.

That doesn’t mean you can’t find history here. Lechuga’s Italian Restaurant has been around since 1961, and My Brother’s Bar (add a burger to your beer order) is the city’s oldest bar—it’s been operating since 1873.

Imbibers can stroll almost anywhere in the ’hood and find plenty of venues to enjoy craft brews (Denver Beer Co.) or craft cocktails (Lady Jane, Room for Milly) or locally made spirits (Mythology Distillery, the Family Jones Spirit House) or coffee (Queensberry Coffee, Pinwheel Coffee).

The district's interesting blend of urban charm and unique industrial revival makes it a great destination for visitors. Historic warehouses and factories now house jazz bars, restaurants, brewpubs, art galleries and working studios. RiNo boasts a diverse mix of creative businesses ranging from visual artists, designers and furniture makers, to craft distillers and brewers, winemakers, creators of unique outdoor gear and small-batch coffee roasters. The art definitely extends beyond gallery walls in this neighborhood, with its colorful and innovative street art murals in alleys and on buildings around almost every corner!

name: Tiki Townhouse-RiNo District-Close to Everything!
neighborhood_overview:
The River North Art District "where art is made" goes by the nickname of "RiNo" and has even adopted a rhino design for its official logo, so look for creative rhinos in art and signage all around the neighborhood!

The district's interesting blend of urban charm and unique industrial revival makes it a great destination for visitors. Historic warehouses and factories now house jazz bars, restaurants, brewpubs, art galleries and working studios.

RiNo boasts a diverse mix of creative businesses ranging from visual artists, designers and furniture makers, to craft distillers and brewers, winemakers, creators of unique outdoor gear and small-batch coffee roasters. The art definitely extends beyond gallery walls in this neighborhood, with its colorful and innovative street art murals in alleys and on buildings around almost every corner!

Lonely Planet named RiNo one of the top 10 neighborhoods to visit in the U.S.

name: 2 bdrm home in City Park West
neighborhood_overview:
There is plenty to do within walking distance from the house - City Park, which includes Denver Zoo and City Park Golf Course, is a few blocks to the east and there are a number of bars and restaurants all over to the south.

For restaurants, I recommend Atelier (French), Pho & Bar (Vietnamese), Dos Santos (tacos), and Spice Room (Indian).

Welcome to your dream getaway in the heart of Denver's historic Santa Fe Arts District, where you'll discover the perfect blend of modern luxury and Rocky Mountain vibes. We're excited to introduce you to this exceptional property and the vibrant neighborhood it calls home.

La Alma Lincoln Park is not only one of Denver’s oldest residential neighborhoods, with a rare concentration of homes built before 1890, but it was also at the heart of Denver’s Chicano Movement, or El Movimiento, in the 1960s and 1970s. The neighborhood demonstrates the close connection between place and people, made tangible by the surviving structures set close together — diverse in their architectural styles yet maintaining a consistent pattern for 150 years. We invite you to explore the streets of your historic neighborhood.

name: King Bed - Private Suite: Walk to Lake, Pickleball
neighborhood_overview:
Discover Denver's hidden gem. The neighborhood is a vibrant mosaic of cultures, offering some of the city’s most authentic Vietnamese and Mexican cuisines—a foodie's paradise verified by my own experiences living in both of these countries. Happy to provide any recommendations for food or other things!

Just a stone's throw away from Huston Lake. Step out to enjoy a game of pickleball with complimentary paddles provided for an active start to your day. For music lovers, the Levitt Pavilion hosts a free summer concert series—perfect for those balmy Denver nights under the stars.

When winter's chill sets in, Ruby Hill offers the quintessential Colorado experience with its popular sledding hills. Golf enthusiasts will appreciate the proximity to Overland Golf Course, offering lush fairways and challenging greens.

Exploration is easy here—South Broadway's eclectic mix of entertainment and downtown Denver's vibrant nightlife are just a quick rideshare away.

Stretching along Santa Fe Drive, this neighborhood boasts a dynamic array of art galleries, studios, and exhibition spaces showcasing everything from traditional to contemporary artworks. A focal point is the First Friday Art Walk, where galleries open their doors to the public, creating a bustling atmosphere with live performances, food trucks, and a chance to meet local artists. The district is also adorned with colorful street art and murals, adding to its creative charm and providing a canvas for artistic expression. Throughout the year, the Santa Fe Art District hosts cultural events and festivals that celebrate art, music, and the community's rich diversity. Beyond art, visitors can explore a variety of dining options, from cozy cafes to trendy eateries, making it a vibrant destination for both art lovers and those seeking to experience Denver's cultural heartbeat.

From world-renowned brands to one-of-a-kind local boutiques, Cherry Creek Shopping Center is Denver’s fashion destination. Plus, enjoy special events and entertainment throughout the year. The shopping center is also home to a dine-in movie theater with reclining heated seats, as well as popular dining spots like Kona Grill, 801 Chophouse and Elway’s. Complimentary luggage storage is available at Valet Plaza and free Wi-Fi and charging stations are available throughout the shopping center.

name: Serenity at Sloan's, 1-BR with a Modern Twist
neighborhood_overview:
Sloan’s Lake/West Colfax No matter what you’re planning on doing, we are close to it all. Walk to Sloan’s Lake Park, delicious brews, rock star restaurants and Alamo Drafthouse, an excellent movie theater that also shows classic films and offers cocktails and food served seat-side.

name: Urban Cottage in Denver’s RiNo District
neighborhood_overview:
The River North Art District "where art is made" goes by the nickname of "RiNo" and has even adopted a rhino design for its official logo. Look for creative rhinos in art and signage all around the neighborhood!

The district's interesting blend of urban charm and unique industrial revival makes it a great destination for visitors. Historic warehouses and factories now house jazz bars, restaurants, brewpubs, art galleries and working studios.

RiNo boasts a diverse mix of creative businesses ranging from visual artists, designers and furniture makers, to craft distillers and brewers, winemakers, creators of unique outdoor gear and small-batch coffee roasters. The art definitely extends beyond gallery walls in this neighborhood, with its colorful and innovative street art murals in alleys and on buildings around almost every corner!

name: The Mayor's Manor. Timeless Arts and Crafts beauty
neighborhood_overview:
What's To Love About Park Hill

Designed to showcase Mayor Speer's City Beautiful program, Park Hill, located on high ground east of City Park, remains one of the most coveted neighborhoods in Denver. Shaded by stately American Elms, Park Hill's exquisite thoroughfares: 17th Avenue, Forest, and Montview parkways, are among the most beautiful in the city.

In addition to an abundance of mature trees, 17th Avenue Parkway, designed by noted landscape architect Fredrick Law Olmsted, boasts a lush landscaped median and generous setbacks. Many of the neighborhood's first residences were designed by Fisher and Fisher, for decades one of the most distinguished architectural firms in Denver.

Early on, commentators raved that the thoroughfares of Park Hill -- "the most desirable residence portion of the city" -- rivaled Riverside Drive in New York, the Auteil and Passy in Paris, and Mayfair in London. Several of Denver's most beautiful churches are also found here.

An influx of new eateries and shops (and a light rail stop just across its eastern border) has brought more foot traffic—and driven ongoing conversations about gentrification. Home prices have subsequently increased 25 percent between 2021 and 2022; average single-family homes are now approaching $900,000 in the historically immigrant community.

Only one of its five schools received top marks, but the northern district—which has held on to its strong Italian and Hispanic influences—benefits from its convenient location, walkability, appealing blend of charming bungalows and Tudors with more recent townhome additions, and strong community (the neighborhood even hosts an annual music festival).

neighborhood_overview:
Curtis Park is one of the city’s oldest and most diverse residential areas. The neighborhood’s heyday was from the late 1870s until 1893. The district is a showcase of architectural styles from that era, including Italianate, Queen Anne, and Victorian eclectic homes. Nestled among these mansions is our "Mini Mansion". We are just a half mile walk to the heart of RiNo Art District, with its lively street art, breweries, coffee shops, and shopping. Walking distance to many restaurants, shops, and downtown attractions.

In the heart of Curtis Park you will find Mestizo-Curtis Park. This hot spot has an outdoor pool, playground, and tall beautiful trees. You will also find a soccer, tennis, and a baseball court. St. Joseph hospital is located only a couple blocks away. When you visit the Curtis Park area you will also want to visit the Casino Cabaret where some of the best jazz musicians in the country have shows.

neighborhood_overview: The Santa Fe Art District in Denver is a vibrant cultural enclave renowned for its diverse artistic offerings. Stretching along Santa Fe Drive, this neighborhood boasts a dynamic array of art galleries, studios, and exhibition spaces showcasing everything from traditional to contemporary artworks. A focal point is the First Friday Art Walk, where galleries open their doors to the public, creating a bustling atmosphere with live performances, food trucks, and a chance to meet local artists. The district is also adorned with colorful street art and murals, adding to its creative charm and providing a canvas for artistic expression. Throughout the year, the Santa Fe Art District hosts cultural events and festivals that celebrate art, music, and the community's rich diversity. Beyond art, visitors can explore a variety of dining options, from cozy cafes to trendy eateries, making it a vibrant destination for both art lovers and those seeking to experience Denver's cultural heartbeat.

name: *Hist. Platt Park Hm|2 Blks to Pearl St|Lrg Yard*
neighborhood_overview:
Platt Park, named after the nearby James H. Platt's nursery, has a rich history dating back to the late 19th century. Originally a part of the Town of South Denver, it was annexed to the City of Denver in 1886. The area experienced significant development during the early 20th century, witnessing the construction of Craftsman-style homes and bungalows that still dot the streets today, showcasing the architectural trends of that era.

One notable feature is the Old South Pearl Street commercial district, a historic area that has evolved into a vibrant hub. The district maintains some of its original buildings, providing a glimpse into the neighborhood's commercial past. Platt Park also boasts the charming Platt Park itself, a public green space that has been a focal point for community gatherings and events over the years.

name: Newly Built Cook Street Carriage House
neighborhood_overview:
The Carriage House is located in the Congress Park neighborhood, a historic streetcar suburb where most of the housing stock was built between 1900 and the 1920s. The area predominantly features brick Craftsman bungalows, with brick Denver Square houses more common to the north. Aside from the restaurants and shops on 12th Avenue, the former streetcar route, the neighborhood is primarily residential. With a canopy of mature trees and sidewalks throughout, it is perfect for walking.

A block and a half north is Colfax Avenue (US 40) and the Bluebird District. Anchored by the Bluebird Theater, the district is composed of restaurants, bars, breweries, cafes and shops, providing more of an urban edge.

Wander through streets adorned with colorful murals and discover a plethora of art galleries, craft breweries, and unique eateries.
